mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% over the prior quarter is interpreted by market participants as a signal of tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces expected equity valuations, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < PAYEMS growth rate over the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when the labor strength signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) relative to GDP (INDPRO) indicates pent-up demand in the economy, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds INDPRO growth rate by > 2% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative when the demand signal is strong (rolling IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side headwinds, which typically precede a decline in corporate earnings estimates and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO shows a downward trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 60-day mean during supply contractions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, market expectations for future rate cuts are reduced, lowering risk-free rates and supporting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% and remains above for at least 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when inflation is above 2% for > 2 months (rolling IC > 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS) indicates a labor market imbalance favoring supply, which can trigger a bearish reaction in equities over the next 5 days as investors anticipate slower hiring.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 20% in a month while PAYEMS increases by < 10%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such imbalances.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% and FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for two consecutive months, a dual signal of weak labor and patient monetary policy is generated, which historically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: low inflation and loose policy regime
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in retail sales (not available in the provided proxies – thus this sketch is omitted to strictly follow the proxy rule). Instead, a supply-focused always-on signal: A continuous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three months is interpreted as structural supply weakness, which tends to depress earnings expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such contractions are not statistically lower than the 60-day mean (p > 0.05).
